description: Scrolls a page from its top at a steady pace, 1.25 screens a second, and records how it behaves: where the screen holds while its content plays, what fades, slides, scales or is uncovered, and whether it glides on or plays once when the scroll stops. The scroll is cut into scenes. Writes a PDF (an overview and a page per scene with six frames from its entry to its exit), a .json beside it with every scene measured, and each scene's six frames as JPEGs in a .frames folder. Use it to rebuild a page's scroll animations, or to show them without a video. The result is that JSON, every frame with its absolute path, and the files' paths. The scan takes up to two minutes; a tabId is scrolled where the user sees it, and their touching the page or the popup's Stop ends it early with what it had (ended says so). A tall page or a long list can take minutes. When the answer has status "running", the capture is still going in the browser: call this tool again with exactly the same arguments to wait for its result, and do not start another capture of that tab meanwhile.

browserId.description: Which browser to act on, from list_browsers. Optional when only one is connected. Chrome runs a separate extension per profile, so a work profile and a personal profile are two different browsers.

outputPath.description: Where to write the PDF. A directory keeps the suggested name, <title>-storyboard-<day>.pdf; the .json and the .frames folder go beside it, named after it. A leading ~ is the home directory. Defaults to the working directory, or to ~/Downloads when that cannot be written.

tabId.description: A tab from list_tabs, scrolled where the user can see it. Give one of tabId or url.

timeoutSeconds.description: How long the browser may take, in seconds. Default 240: the scan scrolls for up to two minutes, then the PDF is built. Not how long this call waits (see the tool description).

url.description: Opens a background tab on this address, scans its scroll, and closes it again. Give one of tabId or url.

viewport.description: The viewport to scan at, in CSS px. A tab opened for url is scanned at 1440 by 900 without it; a tabId at its window's size, and put back after one.

waitSeconds.description: How long to wait for a browser to connect, in seconds. Chrome retires the extension after about thirty seconds of silence, so the default covers the reconnect. 0 fails immediately.

windowId.description: Which window to open `url` in, from list_tabs. Ignored when tabId is given.

name: storyboard_page
title: Scan a page's scroll as a storyboard
